title: Modifying Driver Behavior with Callbacks
description: Inject an error and a delay into a driver using a callback hook without altering the driver class itself.

steps.title: Step 1: Review the Hook
steps.instructions: Open `testbench.sv` and locate the `packet_driver_cb` virtual class, the `uvm_do_callbacks` call inside the driver's `run_phase`, and the `a_parity_ok` checker in `packet_if`. Note which packet fields the driver reads after the hook returns.

steps.title: Step 2: Implement the Callback
steps.instructions: Create a class `error_inject_cb` extending `packet_driver_cb`. Override the function `pre_drive(packet_driver driver, packet pkt)` to set `pkt.inject_parity_error = 1` and `pkt.extra_delay_cycles = 2`.

steps.title: Step 3: Attach in the Test
steps.instructions: In `my_test::connect_phase` (not `build_phase`: `env.drv` is still null there, and `add(null, cb)` would register the callback type-wide), create the callback and attach it with `uvm_callbacks#(packet_driver, packet_driver_cb)::add(env.drv, my_cb)`. Run: each of the three packets should show a `CB` message, `error=1 delay_cycles=2` in the `DRV` line, and one `PARITY_ERR` error.
